subject: Airgap packaging, module idempotency, and CI safety retro
messages:
From: Tim Owers <tim.owers@acme-corp.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: InfraOps <infraops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deploy: airgap packaging + idempotency evidence request

Sergio,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As we prepare our security review for a private (airgapped) deployment of Redwood in our datacenter, the SecOps and Infra teams have asked for concrete evidence that: 1) Terraform/Helm/Ansible modules are idempotent and recoverable, 2) packaging for offline installs (images/artifacts) is repeatable and signed, and 3) CI/CD gating prevents regressions.

Can you share your recommended artifacts and a short checklist we can include in our audit packet? Ideally we want:
- a packaging artifact (tar + checksums) for helm charts and operator manifests
- OCI image tarballs with signed digests or attestations
- a reproducible idempotency test run (terraform apply/destroy cycles, helm upgrade idempotency) with outputs
- CI job names that gate merges for private deployments

We have a 2027-09-20 window for internal audit review — can you help us assemble this by 2027-09-14 so we can circulate? Attached is our initial requirements doc.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Owers
Infra Architect, Acme Financial

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Tim Owers <tim.owers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: InfraOps <infraops@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: airgap packaging + idempotency evidence request

Tim — thanks, and great summary. We'll own producing the audit packet. Quick plan: internal pre-review this week, deliverables by 2027-09-13 (one day earlier than you asked) so you have time to circulate.

High-level approach:
- Packaging: we’ll produce an airgap bundle per release (helm charts, operator manifests, CRDs, and a tar of OCI images). Each bundle will include sha256 checksums and a signing statement (currently using Cosign + in-house key management; we can provide verification steps).
- Idempotency evidence: run our idempotency harness that executes terraform apply -> terraform plan (no changes) -> terraform destroy, and the same for helm (helm upgrade --install twice, compare manifests). We version the harness results and attach logs.
- CI gating: add an "airgap-e2e" pipeline which must pass on the release branch; it runs the idempotency harness in a sandbox with mocked networking.

Immediate owners / asks:
- Irene: lead idempotency runs and attach logs (owner: Irene Choi)
- Mina: package builder for airgap bundles, produce checksums and signing (owner: Mina Haddad)
- Laura: KMS/key attestation and doc for verifying signatures (owner: Laura Bennett)

Tim, could you confirm the audit contact and whether we should include encrypted payloads for your internal registry, or plain tarballs will suffice? Also, any special requirements for artifact signing (specific CAs or HSM)?

Irene/Mina/Laura — I'll schedule a 30-min review tomorrow to walk through the checklist and assign PRs.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Owers <tim.owers@acme-corp.com>, InfraOps <infraops@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-09-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: airgap packaging + idempotency evidence request

Sergio / team — quick technical notes from the idempotency harness I ran this morning (attached results: idempotency-test-results-20270905.csv). Key items: 

- Terraform modules: we execute a randomized state seed and run apply -> plan -> apply (idempotency check) -> destroy. We assert zero-diff on the plan after the second apply. Known caveat: resources with provider-side generated names (some storage classes) need explicit name pinning; flagged modules show that and Mina will update templates.

- Helm charts: run helm upgrade --install twice with --atomic disabled for the second run to compare rendered manifests. Ensure chart hooks are either suppressed or deterministic; non-deterministic hooks (pre-install jobs that create nonce resources) are wrapped in a deterministic helper.

- Ansible roles: use ansible-playbook --check and a subsequent converge run; ephemeral inputs (timestamps) are normalized before comparison.

- Images and packaging: OCI images are exported via skopeo to tar, digests recorded; we use cosign to produce a signature for each image and for the bundle tar.gz. The CI job uploads artifacts to a secure S3 bucket (for hosted) and produces an alternate signed-tar for airgap installs.

- CI gating: pipeline "airgap-e2e" (refs: PR #421) runs the harness inside a container that simulates disconnected networks and verifies tarball checksums and cosign verification. If any idempotency check fails, the pipeline opens a blocking issue and prevents merge.

Action items I can pick up this week: run the full harness against the release branch and attach the logs; add a short README to the packaging-checklist.md explaining verification steps.

On the external question: Tim, if you require HSM-backed attestations instead of cosign key files, we can provide an integration plan; please let us know the KMS vendor.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Staff Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Tim Owers <tim.owers@acme-corp.com>, InfraOps <infraops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy: airgap packaging + idempotency evidence request

Tim — summary and next steps: thanks for the prompt turnaround. We will deliver the audit packet by 2027-09-13 and have included the following in the bundle:

- acme-airgap-requirements.pdf (your original ask)
- packaging-checklist.md (verification steps and commands for cosign + tar verification)
- idempotency-test-results-20270905.csv (Irene's harness run)
- airgap-bundle-release-20270913.tar.gz (signed, will be delivered to the secure transfer URL)

Decisions / confirmations:
- Signing: default is cosign signatures stored alongside artifacts. If you require HSM-backed attestations, Laura will own an HSM integration plan.
- Artifact format: tar.gz with sha256 checksums + cosign signatures. We will also provide an encrypted variant for your internal registry import tool if you request it.
- CI gate: "airgap-e2e" must pass on release branches. PR #421 will include the pipeline definition and the test harness wrapper.

Open items for you:
1) Please confirm whether encrypted tarballs are required for transfer, and if so share the public key or KMS details.
2) Grant a short-term whitelist for our test runner IPs to access your fallback registry if we need to validate digests during the run.

Proposed short sync: 2027-09-08 at 10:00 PT, 30 mins to walk the artifacts and verification steps. I'll send a calendar invite pending your confirmation.

Thanks — we'll attach the artifacts to the ticket and share the Drive link when the bundle is ready.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
